prose_updates.tldr: Randomization identifies the two ordinal potential-outcome marginals but not their coupling. The note characterizes every shortest coupling-robust individual-effect set as a high-mass difference set, gives an exact boundary-safe ternary disconnectedness frontier, and proves a sharp missed elbow in the price of interval reporting: the worst multiplicative price is \((2L-1)/3\) when target coverage exceeds one half and \(L/2\) when target coverage is at most one half. The interval benchmark is the shortest completion of the anchor's marginal-robust validity criterion; comparison is direct on the anchor's stated coverage-level domain and extends the same functional through its omitted neighborhood and the elbow. Exact min-cut computation and simultaneous multinomial confidence-polytopes provide finite-sample certification and uniform selector recovery away from explicit tie surfaces.

project_justification.gap: The closest ITE papers give sharp distributional bounds and discuss marginal-robust interval reports, but no located result formulates and solves the general ordinal shortest-interval oracle, solves the outer cardinality optimization over arbitrary effect sets, or identifies the coverage-level elbow in their sharp comparison. Hall theory certifies a fixed support but does not solve either selection problem.
project_justification.niche: Ordinal outcomes create integer difference geometry in which disconnected sets can be dramatically shorter than the shortest interval induced by the same every-compatible-coupling validity requirement, with the maximal penalty changing exactly when target coverage crosses one half.
project_justification.fill: The difference-set normal form, explicit interval-validity bridge, complete ternary frontier, sharp two-regime general-support interval price with matching equality systems, and confidence-polytope inversion jointly deliver identification, geometry, computation, and honest reporting.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Richardson (2025), Sections 3 and Appendix D, discuss coupling-robust prediction intervals and the ordinal case, while Section 5 supplies sharp bounds for a single individual-effect probability mass. They do not formulate or optimize the general ordinal shortest-interval oracle. The present note minimizes cardinality, equivalently integer endpoint length, over intervals satisfying their marginal-robust validity requirement and then compares that induced benchmark with arbitrary effect sets. This is a direct comparison on their stated coverage-level domain; on their omitted neighborhood of one-half, including \(\alpha=1/2\), it is an extension of the same validity functional. Fan and Park (2010) are the direct sharp distribution-of-ITE comparator: they derive Makarov-type distribution-function bounds and inference, whereas the present target selects a shortest common-coupling set of effect values and characterizes when that set is disconnected. Koperberg (2024) supplies finite Strassen--Hall deficiency for a fixed relation and is used only as identification machinery. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive sharp scalar ordinal benefit bounds through cumulative transportation arguments; the present target is a common-coupling multi-diagonal set. Gao, Shan, Srinivas, and Vijayaraghavan (2025) motivate measuring the price of geometric restrictions, but their structured conformal sets are evaluated under an observed outcome law rather than an adversarial potential-outcome coupling. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021) motivate simplex confidence-region inversion, Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2019) address nonregular scalar ordinal-bound inference, and Fang and Santos (2019) explain why active-set ties require directional methods. Duarte and coauthors (2024) motivate exhaustive discrete computation but do not replace the symbolic frontier. Goldman and coauthors (2020) supply the seven-category randomized endpoint for the concrete application.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Hall identity is established prior machinery specialized to this problem. The contribution is the optimizer-wide difference-set geometry, the shortest-interval completion of the marginal-robust validity criterion, the exhaustive ternary frontier, and the proved sharp interval-price phase transition with computable equality regimes. Comparison with Zhang and Richardson (2025) is direct only on their stated coverage-level domain; conclusions in the omitted neighborhood of one-half and at \(\alpha=1/2\) extend the same functional. The extremal marginal laws certify worst-case constants and are not asserted to equal the empirical law in the remdesivir trial. The confidence result is finite-sample honest but makes no efficiency claim. Selector recovery is asserted only on \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\); exact recovery on tie surfaces is not claimed, and a fixed prescribed \(\eta\) excludes positive-width neighborhoods even though failure of existence of some positive margin is confined to finitely many affine surfaces. When \(L=2\), the reduction agrees with Zhang and Richardson's result that the sole disconnected candidate cannot be shortest, providing the binary sanity check.
